item.title: Ocelot 0.3.9
item.description:
• Phone frame in Preview. Mobile screens now show inside a phone, island included, and scroll inside it. Turn it off with the phone button in the Preview bar.
  • Try any width in Preview. The width button in the Preview bar renders the screen at a phone, tablet or desktop width, or at a width you type, and the layout reflows as far as the design allows.
  • Website mockups come alive. The agent now gives every button, link, card and input hover, pressed and focus states, gives the hero an entrance, and adds one signature animation where the brief earns it.

item.title: Ocelot 0.3.8
item.description:
• Long agent conversations keep working. Screenshots of whole pages are sent to the model smaller, the agent drops older screenshots after a busy turn and compacts the conversation on its own when it gets long. A conversation that has become too large compacts itself and asks you to send your message again, instead of failing with "413".
  • Compact button in the Agent tab: a summary replaces older messages and screenshots, and the agent keeps the gist.
  • Preview switches between sizes. When a screen has a desktop and a mobile version (named like "Home — Desktop" and "Home — Mobile"), the Preview bar shows Desktop / Tablet / Mobile buttons that jump between them.
  • Following several agents no longer jumps around: the camera zooms out once to show everything they are working on and stays there.
  • Contrast is checked in hover, pressed and focus states too, so a button whose label disappears when you point at it is caught. The agent checks contrast in every state before it finishes.
  • Screenshots no longer show photos blank now and then.
  • The agent activity dot sits inside the Agent tab.

item.title: Ocelot 0.3.7
item.description:
• Components. Turn any layer into a component (⌥⌘K, or right-click) and place instances of it anywhere: change the main and every instance follows. Instances can change their text, images, colours and visibility, and components can have props such as a label, a toggle or a variant. Find them in Assets › Components; detach an instance to make it plain layers again. React export writes each component once with typed props, and the agent builds shared parts like a sidebar, nav or buttons as components instead of copies.
  • The agent can work in parallel. For several independent screens it starts helpers that build one screen each, at the same time. Each helper only has Ocelot's own tools and runs inside the agent's sandbox.
  • See and follow every agent. The toolbar shows each working agent; click to see what each one is doing and pick which one the camera follows (or all). Every agent's work is marked on the canvas in its own colour.
  • Ask the agent about a layer. Select a layer and click the small button next to it (⇧⌘K): write what should change and add it to the chat, or send it right away. The agent gets exactly that layer.
  • Task systems pick their display font deliberately: Geist stays for text, and an editorial, warm or playful brief gets a fitting display face.
  • Privacy: the sandboxed agent now only ever sees a copy of the conversation it is working on, never your other conversations.

item.title: Ocelot 0.3.6
item.description:
• Conversation history in the agent sidebar. "+" starts a new conversation and keeps the old one; the clock button lists this document's conversations, and opening one continues it with everything the agent knew. Conversations are kept when you close the window or quit, stay outside the document (sharing a file never shares your chats), and can be deleted.
  • No accidental stops: starting a new conversation, or switching, while the agent is working asks first.
  • A design system made for the task. When a document has no style yet and you give no direction, the agent first creates one for this project: named colours, fonts and corner radii, saved with the document. Everything it draws uses them, so changing a colour or font in Assets › Styles restyles the whole design. Agents can do the same with create_theme.

item.title: Ocelot 0.3.5
item.description:
• Pasted and attached images and files show up in the agent sidebar again, with their remove button. They were added but invisible.
  • The agent's name in the toolbar while it works is a quiet indicator again, not a box that looked like a tab.
  • Token chips in the Tokens and Assets panels are visible again.

item.title: Ocelot 0.3.4
item.description: • A long paste in the agent sidebar becomes a tidy one-line chip again: "Paste as text" no longer wraps onto two lines.

item.title: Ocelot 0.3.3
item.description:
• Install Command-Line Tool now also puts ocelot on your PATH, so it works in the next terminal window you open, without editing your shell profile.
  • Settings › Updates no longer shows a paragraph of fine print.

item.title: Ocelot 0.3.2
item.description:
• New: Patterns, under Assets › Patterns. 13 written specs for common product screens (sign in, onboarding, settings, dashboards, tables, detail pages, search, empty states, notifications, pricing, upgrade, checkout, permission prompts). Each lists the states to draw, copy rules, sizes and the mistakes to avoid. "Build with agent" hands one to the agent, optionally with a line about your product.
  • Agents can look up the same patterns (list_patterns, get_pattern, which also matches a plain description such as "billing page") and read a new guide on product screens: one artboard per state (first use, no results, error, no access, loading) and one label per action.
  • Inspection can now compare artboards on a page: the same action labelled differently, too many corner radii, and data screens missing their loading, empty or error state.

item.title: Ocelot 0.3.1
item.description: • Copies of Ocelot 0.2 now update to this version automatically. Version 0.3.0 was numbered in a way that made earlier copies skip it; everything in 0.3.0 is included here.

item.title: Ocelot 0.3.0
item.description:
Ocelot is now open source under the GNU AGPL-3.0. Updates come straight from this repository and no longer need a GitHub sign-in.

Watch the agent design

  • Each part the agent writes plays onto the canvas: an outline in the agent's colour, then the content top to bottom. A marker shows what it is writing ("Writing Hero"), and the view follows work that happens off screen, without pulling the view away while you scroll.
  • With the built-in agent, a section grows on the canvas while the agent is still writing it, then settles into real layers in a single undo step.
  • The agent is present from the moment you press Send. Steps in the sidebar say what was built ("Hero: headline and booking card"), and badges name the agent ("Claude is editing").

Work with the agent

  • Ask, queue and steer: agents can ask you multiple-choice questions; Enter queues a message while the agent works, ⌘↩ steers it mid-turn.
  • Attach images, text files and long pastes to a prompt, in the sidebar and on Home.
  • Image generation runs in the background while the agent keeps building. Choose the default image model in Settings › Images.
  • Hand off to an agent (Export menu): copy a prompt for a coding agent, or save a folder with screenshots, React code, the design system and the motion, so the design gets implemented as drawn.
  • Every action in the app is available to agents over MCP, including opening Ocelot, creating and saving projects, and changing settings. Security settings stay yours.

Design systems

  • Build your own design system on shadcn/ui with Base UI: eight styles, colours, radius, fonts and icons, light and dark, with a token editor that checks contrast.
  • About 60 components and 23 blocks (login, sign-up, sidebar layouts) become real layers on the canvas: change a token and every instance follows.
  • Tweak individual components, paste or copy shadcn preset codes, and export a shadcn registry or React code with real component imports.
  • A Design system page shows every foundation and component.

Better designs out of the box

  • Geist is the default type family, including Geist Serif and Geist Pixel.
  • Agents follow tighter guidance on layout, calm type, real imagery and motion, and a built-in inspection flags layout defects and unintended defaults.
  • Screens that belong together are linked, so you can click through them in Preview.

Everyday details

  • Real tooltips, a fully keyboard-accessible Layers panel (⇧⌘L locks, ⇧⌘H hides), and "Back to content" when you have panned away from everything.
  • Calmer motion throughout the app, with reduced motion respected everywhere.
  • Opening a document from Finder or the command line now works in every case.
  • Home moves to ⇧⌘1.
